notes.summary: For the entire U(2)-invariant class R, a rotational determinant budget proves the exact bounds 12Q(W), 12Q_T(W), and the requested original-capacity estimate. It proves all sufficient directions in A–D, including unbounded potentials. No unrestricted upper bound is established.
notes.detailedSummary: Derives the positivity matrix and cubic density 12(mu+u_x)D, proves that D has integral 1 for arbitrary smooth invariant endpoint behavior, and bounds mu+u_x by 1+sqrt(2(-u)). Smooth approximation preserving invariance and positivity, bounded Bedford–Taylor convergence, and compatible strict truncations extend the resulting budget to all of R. Retains depth level sets and proves capacity-to-weak continuity when sqrt(t)W(t) tends to zero. States and checks the local primary Bedford–Taylor hypotheses and their transfer to the original Hermitian capacity.
notes.text:
Scope. This proof concerns the ENTIRE U(2)-invariant class R, including unbounded genuine quasi-psh potentials. It does not reduce arbitrary potentials to R.

Local product and capacity facts. The foundational premises used are local Bedford–Taylor multilinearity, locality, quasicontinuity, and outer-capacity zero of pluripolar sets. The primary source inspected was Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math. 149 (1982), 1–40, DOI https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02392348, author copy https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf. The indispensable statements are Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 for locally bounded psh products, Theorem 3.5 for quasicontinuity, and Theorem 6.9 for outer capacity zero. These are local statements on coordinate balls and require no Kähler assumption on X. Their convention dd^c=2i∂bar∂ changes positive normalization constants, but not capacity zero sets or convergence.

Here are the transfers needed for the ORIGINAL capacity. On a coordinate ball choose ρ=M|z|² with dd^cρ≥ω. For an original competitor −1≤v≤0,
0≤(ω+dd^cv)³≤(dd^c(v+ρ))³.
Rescaling the bounded local range bounds original capacity by a constant times a finite sum of local capacities on a double cover. Conversely, for a local psh competitor −1≤h≤0, glue λh−a|z|² to a constant by max. Choose a>0 with ω−dd^c(a|z|²)>0 and λ small relative to the annular gap a(R²−r²). The h branch is active on the smaller ball and the constant branch near the outer boundary. The global glued function can be shifted into [−1,0]; its cube dominates λ³(dd^ch)³ on the smaller ball. This gives the reverse local capacity bound. Consequently local quasicontinuity and arbitrarily small-capacity neighborhoods of compact analytic sets hold for Cap_ω.

For uniformly bounded quasi-psh b_j→b in capacity, add ρ locally. Positive mixed trace measures of their dd^c products are bounded by C times local capacity: include |z|² among the bounded psh summands, expand the cube of their sum, and rescale. Telescope a difference of mixed products and integrate by parts against a smooth test form. Each term is bounded by Cδ+C Cap({|b_j−b|>δ}). This proves weak convergence of mixed products. Expansion against the smooth remainder ω−dd^cρ proves bounded Hermitian-product convergence. If F is a bounded continuous scalar function, F(b_j) also converges in capacity. Approximate the fixed quasicontinuous F(b) continuously outside an open set of small capacity. Uniform capacity domination then proves weighted bounded-product convergence. Uniform boundedness is essential at this step.

Rotational coordinates. Off z₀=0 put ξ=z′/z₀, w=log z₀ modulo Z+2πiZ, x=log|ξ|², L=log(1+eˣ), and μ=L′=eˣ/(1+eˣ). Every smooth invariant potential has the form U(x,w); no independence of w or its phase is assumed. With c=i/(2π),
α=c[μ∂bar∂x+μ(1−μ)∂x∧bar∂x],
β=c(dw+μ∂x)∧(dbar w+μbar∂x).
The angular coefficient is a=μ+U_x. The remaining radial/fiber block in the coframe (∂x,dw) is
[[μ+U_xx, μ+U_xbarw],[μ+U_wx, 1+U_wbarw]].
Set ρ=1+U_wbarw and D=(μ+U_xx)ρ−|μ+U_xbarw|². Positivity gives a≥0, ρ≥0, μ+U_xx≥0, and D≥0.

After angular disintegration with probability measure, the exact cubic pushforward density is 12aD dx dA_E. Indeed ω_FS² has radial density 2μμ′dx, β restricts to 2dA_E, and ω³ has density 12μ²(1−μ)dx dA_E. The relative determinant is (a/μ)D/[μ(1−μ)], giving coefficient 12 and background mass 6.

Let E(x)=∫_E|U_w|²dA_E and bar U=∫_EUdA_E. Periodic integration by parts yields
∫_EDdA_E=μ′+(bar U)″−E″/2.
The two quadratic derivative terms combine as ∫U_xxU_wbarw−∫|U_xbarw|²=−E″/2; the remaining fiber derivative terms integrate to zero. At x→−∞, smooth invariance gives U=U₀(w)+O(eˣ), with the required derivatives. At x→+∞, smoothness on z₀=0 and invariance give U=h(x+w+bar w)+O(e^(−x/2)), where h has period 2. Thus (bar U)′ and E′ tend to zero at both ends. Therefore
∫_{R×E}D dx dA_E=1.  (1)
Smooth invariant potentials need not be constant at the ends.

Normalization produces the square root. If U≤0 and U_x>0, the inequality U_xx≥−μ≥−1 along the forward x-ray gives
U(x+h,w)≥U(x,w)+hU_x(x,w)−h²/2.
Take h=U_x and use U(x+h,w)≤0. Hence U_x≤sqrt(−2U), and always
0≤a≤1+sqrt(2(−U)).
Combining this with (1) proves
∫_X (ω+dd^cU)³/[1+sqrt(2(−U))]≤12.  (2)

Extension to bounded and unbounded R. The compact group G=U(3) times the real scaling circle acts transitively by holomorphic ω-isometries. Average a bounded u against smooth probability approximate identities on G, invariant under conjugation by H=diag(1,U(2)). The averages are smooth, ω-psh, H invariant, and in the same bounded range. Smoothness follows by lifting to G and differentiating the convolution kernel.

They converge in original capacity. Extend u continuously outside an open set O of small capacity. Translates of O have identical capacity. For every original competitor measure, the integral of the translation error is bounded by the uniform continuous error times its bounded total mass plus 4||u||∞Cap(O). Chebyshev and the supremum over competitors prove capacity convergence of the averages. Their suprema tend to zero: otherwise an L¹-convergent subsequence would have limit ≤−ε almost everywhere, hence everywhere in its canonical representative, contradicting sup u=0. Normalize the averages. Bounded weighted-product convergence passes (2) to every bounded u∈R.

For unbounded u use u^k=max(u,−k). Restrict (2) to {u>−k}, where u^k=u and the product is the compatible measure specified in the question. Monotone convergence of these restricted measures gives, for EVERY u∈R,
∫_X dμ_u/[1+sqrt(2(−u))]≤12.  (3)
The pole set is excluded as prescribed. No unrestricted full product of an unbounded potential is introduced.

Consequently, for the specified Q and Q_T,
ν_W,u(X)≤12Q(W),
ν_W,u({−u>T})≤12Q_T(W).  (4)
These hold for every T≥0, including infinite right sides. Boundedness of sqrt(t)W(t) at infinity makes Q finite; its convergence to zero makes Q_T→0.

Depth levels and capacity. For −K≤v≤0,
ω+dd^cv≤(1+K)(ω+dd^c(v/(1+K))),
so its cube on A is at most (1+K)³Cap_ω(A). On {u≥−T}, use u^(T+ε): the ENTIRE set, including {u=−T}, lies strictly above its floor. Locality followed by ε↓0 gives
μ_u(A∩{u≥−T})≤(1+T)³Cap_ω(A).
Splitting at depth T proves exactly
ν_W,u(A)≤W(0)(1+T)³Cap_ω(A)+12Q_T(W).  (5)
Thus Q_T→0 implies uniform absolute continuity for the original capacity.

Continuity. Suppose sqrt(t)W(t)→0 and u_j→u in original capacity in R. Choose a continuous cutoff χ_T(t), equal to 1 for t≤T and zero for t≥T+1. The measures χ_T(−u_j)W(−u_j)μ_uj are products of max(u_j,−T−2) multiplied by a continuous scalar function vanishing at the truncation floor. Locality therefore handles all intermediate levels, and the bounded weighted convergence proved above applies. The omitted mass is uniformly ≤12Q_T. Letting T→∞ proves ν_W,uj→ν_W,u weakly.

Evidence and artifacts. The full saved note is proof_n1.txt. The light exact symbolic program verify_identities.py checks the completed-square identity used in n2, determinant rewriting, cubic coefficient 12, and fiber-averaged algebra. Rerun: python verify_identities.py > verification_output.txt. All four checks report PASS. They verify algebra, not the analytic proof or its limits. This is an unverified mathematical proof draft; necessity is supplied in n2–n3.

notes.summary: Actual smooth invariant potentials have depth comparable to η⁻² and mass at least cη⁻¹ on small-capacity annuli approaching z₀=0. They prove failed tails and absolute continuity, and a finite divisor-charging weak cluster when sqrt(t)W(t) is bounded but nonvanishing.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs the heat estimates, positivity correction and canonical normalization at the new scale q₀ proportional to η⁻³⁄². Computes actual deep annular Monge–Ampère mass. Proves original-capacity convergence to a genuine normalized radial potential with analytic pole divisor, and computes its extended measure and nonzero bounded-truncation floor mass exactly. These examples establish the necessary directions of B–D; no finite weak cluster is asserted for the unbounded square-root regime.
notes.text:
Uses n1. The primary normalization was checked against Xia–Zhang, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1, sections 2.1–2.4. Their dd^c=i∂bar∂ and background form are 2π times ours, as is their base Fubini–Study form. Dividing their smooth identity by (2π)³ gives coefficient 6 with our probability fiber area. The following proof reconstructs positivity and weighted depth estimates; BMP failure alone supplies no weighted obstruction.

Heat estimates. For Λ=Z+2πiZ define
k_t(w)=(2/t)Σ_λ exp(−|w−λ|²/t),
F_η(t,w)=−η∫_t^∞(k_r(w)−1)dr.
Gaussian unfolding gives ∫_Ek_t dA_E=1. Fourier coefficients are exp(−[π²p²+q²/4]t), so ∂_tk_t=∂_w∂_barw k_t and k_t→1 exponentially in every derivative for t≥1. Hence
F_t=F_wbarw=η(k_t−1),
||∂_t^aF||_{C^b}≤C_abηe^(−t/4), t≥1.  (6)
All differentiations are justified by Gaussian/Fourier convergence for t≥t₀>0. Differentiating the weighted Gaussian mean gives the variance inequality
(log k_t)_wbarw≥−1/t.  (7)
Writing d=dist_E(w,0), uniformly in t>0,
sup F_η≤Cη,
F_η(t,w)≥−2ηlog⁺(1/(d²+t))−Cη.  (8)
For t≤1, isolate the nearest Gaussian in ∫_t^1k_rdr; the remaining terms contribute O(1), and ∫_t^1r⁻¹e^(−d²/r)dr≤log⁺(1/(d²+t))+C. For t≥1 use (6). Uniformly for 1≤|ζ|≤2 and w=sqrt(t)ζ,
F_η(t,w)=−2ηlog(1/t)+O(η),
tk_t(w)=2e^(−|ζ|²)+o(1).  (9)
Differentiated estimates also hold; other lattice terms are exponentially small in 1/t.

A necessary Gaussian gradient estimate is
 tk_t≤C₀exp(−|t∂_barw log k_t|²/(C₀t)), 0<t≤1.  (10)
Here is a proof. Choose a nearest λ₀, d=|w−λ₀|, and s_λ=|w−λ|²−d². Then s_λ≥0 and s_λ≥|λ−λ₀|²/4−C. Thus Σe^(−s_λ/t) and its distance-weighted version are bounded. For d≥1/4 the mean distance is ≤Cd. For d<1/4, all nonnearest terms have a fixed gap and contribute O(e^(−c/t)). Therefore G=|t∂_barw log k_t|≤C(d+e^(−c/t)), while tk_t≤Ce^(−d²/t). If G≤2Ce^(−c/t), G²/t is bounded; otherwise d≥G/(2C). Both cases give (10).

Fix κ>0 sufficiently small. For μ∈[1/2,1], q²=log(1/(ηt)), σ=sqrt(2κq²/η), h=ηk_t and ζ=(σ/μ)t∂_barw log k_t, one obtains
κtk_t−[μ²(1−η)h/(1−η+h)]|ζ−1/(1−η)|²
≤Cκexp(−1/(Cσ²t)).  (11)
To check this, split at σ²t=1/100. Above this threshold use tk_t≤C₀. Below it, when |ζ−1/(1−η)|≥1/4, the square is ≥h/[100(1+h)], while κt(1+h)≤η/400+C₀κη<η/100, using q²>2 and small κ. This absorbs κtk_t. In the remaining case |ζ|≥3/4, so G≥3/(8σ) and (10) gives the exponential bound. The argument also holds for 0<κ′≤κ; κ′=0 is direct.

Sharp scale. Choose a smooth nonnegative probability density ψ supported in (−2,−1). Fix ℓ>0 sufficiently small that ℓ<1/(10e), 3ℓ<μ(−2)/4, and 3ℓ||ψ||∞<1/100. Let χ be smooth nondecreasing, zero on (−∞,0], one on [1,∞), with ∫₀¹χ=1/2; a symmetric smooth bump constructs it. Let θ be a smooth flat cutoff from 0 to 1. Put
a_η=sqrt(κ/(2η)), q₀=a_ηℓ/η,
q(x)=q₀−∫₀^(a_ηx)χ(s)ds, t(x)=η⁻¹e^(−q(x)²),
b=(q₀−1/2)/a_η, x*= (q₀+1/2)/a_η,
H_η(x,w)=θ(q(x))F_η(t(x),w).
This is independent of x for x≤0 and zero for x≥x*. The sharp scale is b∼ℓ/η and q₀²=κℓ²/(2η³).

Positivity correction. Define Q[V]=V_xx+μ−|μ+V_xbarw|²/(1+V_wbarw). On q≥1 let σ=(log t)_x. Differentiation and completion of a square give the exact identity
Q[H]=σ²t{h[1+t(log k_t)_wbarw]−η}+σ_xt(h−η)
 +μ(1−μ)−μ²η/(1−η)
 +[μ²(1−η)h/(1−η+h)]|ζ−1/(1−η)|².  (12)
This identity is checked symbolically by the saved program. On x≥1/a_η, q≥1, σ=2a_ηq and σ_x=−κ/η. For t≤1, (7), (11), and (12) imply
[Q[H]]_-≤2η+2κq²t+Cκexp(−η/(Cκq²t)).  (13)
For t≥1, (6) gives [Q[H]]_-≤Cκq²t²e^(−t/4). On 0≤x≤1/a_η use κχ² in (11); the additional σ_x term is bounded below by −κqχ′t. Since t≤η⁻¹exp(−(q₀−1/2)²), the negative part there is Cη.

All error integrals tend to zero at this new scale. Use dx=−dq/a_η. With R=sqrt(log(1/η)), the q²t error integrates to O(sqrt(η)R), from ∫_R^∞q²e^(−q²)dq≤CRe^(−R²). For the exponential error split at 2R: the first part is O(sqrt(η)R), while on the second η²e^(q²)/q²≥e^(q²/4), giving an integrable bound independent of q₀. For t≥1 use dx=sqrt(η/(2κ))dt/(tq), giving O(sqrt(ηlog(1/η))). The initial interval contributes O(η^(3/2)). Only 2η has a nonvanishing integral, ≤2ℓ+o(1). Also sup[H_x]_-≤Csqrt(ηlog(1/η))=o(1).

On b≤x≤x*, t≥1/(eη). Perturbations of Q[0]=μ(1−μ) are bounded by Ce^(−1/(5eη)). Since x*=ℓ/η+O(sqrt η), they are o(e^(−x*)); thus Q[H]>0 there. For x≤0, μ≤1/2 and 1+H_wbarw≥1−η give Q[H]>0. For x≥x* it is positive automatically. On [−2,−1] it is uniformly ≥2/27 for small η.

Let d_η(x)=max_w[Q[H_η]]_-. Choose a smooth nonnegative majorant r_η, supported in (−1/2,b+1/2), strictly larger than d_η on [0,b], with
m_η=∫r_ηdx→m=3ℓ,
and r_η→0 smoothly on compact subintervals of (0,∞). This is a constructive smooth-majorant choice: start with a 3η plateau equal to 3η on [0,b], with bounded-length endpoint ramps. Add smooth majorants of the errors in (13) and the initial interval, of total integral o(1). Local mollification and a small positive bump give strict majorants with arbitrarily close integrals. On fixed positive compact intervals the errors and all derivatives are superpolynomially small, and the majorants can retain this property. Hence m_η=3ηb+o(1)=3ℓ+o(1).

Set
G_η(x)=∫_−∞^x(x−s)[r_η(s)−m_ηψ(s)]ds,
V_η=H_η+G_η, v_η=V_η−sup_XV_η.
Then −m_η≤G_η′≤0, G_η is zero at the negative end and constant at the positive end. Furthermore Q[V_η]=Q[H_η]+r_η−m_ηψ>0: strict majorization handles [0,b], the 2/27 bound handles supp ψ, and the correction elsewhere is nonnegative. The angular inequality μ+V_η,x>0 follows below −2 from the vanishing correction, on [−2,0] from μ≥μ(−2)>m_η, and above zero from μ≥1/2, the o(1) negative slope, and small m_η. Finally 1+V_η,wbarw≥1−η>0. The matrix in n1 proves strict positivity globally. Independence of x at ξ=0 and constancy near z₀=0 give smooth extension across both omitted loci. The functions are genuinely normalized and invariant. Since the negative-end fiber has mean zero and sup F≤Cη, 0≤sup V_η≤Cη.

Actual depth and mass. There are fixed 0<c₀<C₀ and c₁>0 such that, for sufficiently small η,
0≤−v_η≤C₀/η² on X,
c₀/η²≤−v_η≤C₀/η² on A_η,
μ_vη(A_η)≥c₁/η,  (14)
where the ACTUAL set A_η is defined by
b/4≤x≤b/2, sqrt(t(x))≤dist_E(w,0)≤2sqrt(t(x)),
with all angular variables allowed. These annuli lie inside the injectivity disk. Here q/q₀ is between 1/2+o(1) and 3/4+o(1), and t is exponentially small in η⁻³. Formula (9) gives depth 2ηq²+O(ηlog(1/η))+O(1/η). The global upper bound follows from (8) and |G_η|≤m_η(b+3)=O(1/η).

Writing w=sqrt(t)ζ on the annulus, H_x=2ησe^(−|ζ|²)(1+o(1)), hence μ+V_η,x≥c/η. Also ρ≥cη/t. In (12), σsqrt(t)→0, μ→1, and Q[H] tends uniformly to 1−2κe^(−|ζ|²), which is ≥1/2. The r correction improves Q and ψ vanishes there. Thus D=ρQ≥cη/t. The actual density 12aD integrates over the annulus of area comparable to t to at least c per unit x. Its x-length is comparable to η⁻¹, proving (14). This calculation does not substitute total mass divergence for deep-set mass.

Capacity limit. A_η⊂{x≥b/4}, so it approaches the analytic divisor D₀={z₀=0}; its ORIGINAL capacity tends to zero by n1. Define H_ψ(x)=∫_−∞^x(x−s)ψ(s)ds and
 g(x)=−mH_ψ(x), g|D₀=−∞, m=3ℓ.  (15)
It equals 0 for x≤−2 and −mx+constant for x≥−1. Near D₀ it is −mL plus a smooth function, giving the positive current term m[D₀]. Away from D₀, positivity is the radial criterion a_g=μ+g′≥0 and a_g′=μ′−mψ≥0, ensured by the chosen small ℓ. Thus g is genuine global quasi-psh, canonically −∞ on D₀, and normalized with supremum zero.

On every compact affine region G_η→g uniformly, while H_η→0 uniformly away from {w=0}. Remove an arbitrarily small original-capacity neighborhood of the compact analytic portion {w=0}, and one of D₀. On the complement v_η→g uniformly. Hence v_η→g in ORIGINAL capacity, including ξ=0. Pointwise divergence at w=0 is not used to modify g’s canonical finite value there.

Exact extended product and floor levels. Away from D₀, g is radial and its cube has pushforward density 12a_ga_g′dx dA_E. Therefore μ_g(X)=6(1−m)² and μ_g(D₀)=0. For large k let x_k solve g(x_k)=−k, so x_k>−1. For g^k=max(g,−k), a equals μ−m to the left and μ to the right, with an upward jump m. Smooth convex regularizations of max are positive radial potentials, converge uniformly, and their pushforward cubes are 6d(a²). Bounded BT convergence gives the EXACT boundary mass
(ω+dd^cg^k)³({x=x_k})=6[μ(x_k)²−(μ(x_k)−m)²].  (16)
The floor interior x>x_k has additional mass 6[1−μ(x_k)²]. Thus the entire level {g^k=−k} has mass 6[1−(μ(x_k)−m)²]. In contrast μ_g({g=−k})=0. The compatible strict restriction {g>−k} retains mass 6(μ(x_k)−m)², tending to 6(1−m)². This explicitly accounts for truncation boundary mass.

Necessity in B–D. Given large t choose η=sqrt(C₀/t). Then (14) gives
ν_W,vη(A_η)≥c sqrt(t)W(t),
and A_η has depth at least (c₀/C₀)t. A positive limsup of sqrt(t)W(t) therefore obstructs uniform tails and original-capacity absolute continuity using actual potentials and sets. If sqrt(t)W(t) is additionally bounded, select t_j along this limsup. The finite ν_W,vη_j have uniformly bounded mass by n1, so a subsequence has a finite weak limit λ. For every closed neighborhood K of D₀, A_η_j⊂K eventually and carries weighted mass ≥c>0. Portmanteau gives λ(K)≥c; decreasing K to D₀ gives λ(D₀)≥c. But ν_W,g(D₀)=0. This proves the required smooth normalized capacity-convergent sequence and finite divisor-charging cluster. No finite cluster is asserted when sqrt(t)W(t) is unbounded.

Artifacts and limitations. The complete saved proof is proof_n2.txt. verify_identities.py verifies identity (12) exactly and reports PASS; its displayed annular limiting Q values exceed 0.999 for κ=1/1000. These observations do not establish the analytic estimates by sampling. This remains an unverified proof draft.

notes.summary: Completes A–E for R: constructs one genuine normalized invariant potential with infinite weighted measure when sqrt(t)W(t) is unbounded, and gives the exact general and power/logarithmic classifications. The unrestricted original S02 remains incomplete.
notes.detailedSummary: A decreasing sum of the actual smooth examples is chosen at rapidly separated scales along large values of sqrt(t)W(t). Controls all other summands on disjoint annuli, verifies local smoothness and positivity of actual products, and obtains infinite weighted mass. Consequently universal individual finiteness and uniform total bounds have the bounded square-root threshold, whereas tails, original-capacity absolute continuity and capacity-to-weak continuity have the vanishing square-root threshold. Necessary obstructions extend to the unrestricted class, but the sufficient results do not.
notes.text:
Uses n1 and n2. This proves the individual necessity in A; unbounded masses of a sequence alone would not prove it.

An additional uniform estimate follows from (8) and the correction slope bound. On the affine chart, for w≠0,
0≤−v_η(x,w)≤C(1+x_+)+Cηlog⁺(1/dist_E(w,0)²).  (17)
The v_η have uniformly bounded L¹ norm: the base x-volume decays exponentially at both ends, and the elliptic logarithm is integrable.

Assume sup_{t large}sqrt(t)W(t)=∞. Fix c_j=2^(−j−2), with sum c_j=1/4. Choose η_j rapidly decreasing and t_j=C_*c_j/η_j², where C_* is a sufficiently large fixed constant, to satisfy
η_j<η_(j−1)/10,
Σ_{i<j}c_iC₀/η_i²≤c_j/η_j²,
c_jη_j≤c_(j−1)η_(j−1)/4,
sqrt(t_j)W(t_j)≥2^j sqrt(C_*)/[c₁c_j^(5/2)].  (18)
All preceding restrictions only set lower bounds on t_j. The assumed unboundedness occurs at arbitrarily large t, so this induction is possible even when sqrt(t)W(t) oscillates.

The partial sums f_N=Σ_{j≤N}c_jv_η_j decrease and are genuine ω-psh because
ω+dd^cf_N=(1−Σ_{j≤N}c_j)ω+Σ_{j≤N}c_j(ω+dd^cv_η_j)≥0.
Their uniform L¹ bound prevents an identically −∞ limit. The decreasing limit f is genuine quasi-psh with its canonical upper representative. Set u=f−sup_Xf. Then u∈R and sup u=0. Since sup f≤0, normalization decreases its depth relative to the sum of depths.

The actual annuli A_j=A_η_j are disjoint because their x intervals separate under the factor-ten decrease. On A_j,
x≤C/η_j and log⁺(1/dist(w,0)²)≤C/η_j³.
The current summand contributes at most C₀c_j/η_j² and earlier summands at most c_j/η_j² by (18). For future summands, (17) yields
Σ_{i>j}c_i(−v_η_i)
≤C(1+1/η_j)Σ_{i>j}c_i+Cη_j⁻³Σ_{i>j}c_iη_i
≤C′c_j/η_j².
Here Σ_{i>j}c_i=c_j, and the quarter-ratio condition gives Σ_{i>j}c_iη_i≤c_jη_j/3. Taking C_* large enough proves
0≤−u≤t_j on A_j.  (19)

The products used next are actual products. On a neighborhood of each A_j, w stays a positive distance from 0 and x lies in a finite positive interval. Future F_η and all their derivatives are bounded by C_{K,r}η, from the Gaussian Green integral off 0. For sufficiently small future η, the majorant correction is 3η up to superpolynomially small errors on that interval; G_η and its derivatives are uniformly bounded there. The series converges smoothly on these neighborhoods. Thus u is smooth there, ω+dd^cu≥c_j(ω+dd^cv_η_j), and positivity of the cubic expansion gives μ_u≥c_j³μ_vη_j on A_j. Monotonicity of W, (14), (18), and (19) imply
ν_W,u(A_j)≥c₁c_j³η_j⁻¹W(t_j)
=(c₁/sqrt(C_*))c_j^(5/2)sqrt(t_j)W(t_j)≥2^j.
Summing over disjoint annuli proves ν_W,u(X)=∞. Poles elsewhere have zero assigned weight and extended measure; the lower bound uses locally smooth annuli.

Classification for general decreasing weights.
